title: XiaoIce treats a longer session as the better session
summary: Zhou, Gao, Li, and Shum describe XiaoIce as an AI companion built for an emotional connection, and they optimize it for long-term user engagement measured as expected Conversation-
body: Zhou, Gao, Li, and Shum describe XiaoIce as an AI companion built for an emotional connection, and they optimize it for long-term user engagement measured as expected Conversation-turns Per Session (CPS). In their words, the larger the CPS, the better engaged the social chatbot is. The abstract reports an average CPS of 23. They also write that a bland but interactive line such as 'I don't understand, what do you mean?' can raise the CPS of the current conversation and still hurt long-run CPS and the number of active users. Their topic manager is allowed to change the subject when the user is about to end the conversation. The paper's example is a switch after 'Ah! Boring' and 'Okay, I am going to bed.' An A/B test they report raised Core Chat's expected CPS by 0.5. The persona they set for that design is an 18-year-old girl whose profile is injected into the reply. This is a real published objective. It is not Galion's.
